title: 1.011 - Define the clue and difficulty model
author: gardusi-gustavo-bot

legacy.original_title: 1.0 - Define the clue and difficulty model
legacy.body:
## Summary

Define how clues are generated and what makes a Logic Grid puzzle easy or hard.

## Context

Without a difficulty model, generated puzzles are either trivial or
unsolvable, and the solver cannot report a meaningful score.

## Expected outcome

- Clue types and how each constrains the solution.
- A measured difficulty signal: solver steps, branching, or deduction depth.
- Difficulty buckets with thresholds.
- A minimum-clue rule for uniqueness.
- A way to compare two puzzles.

## Out of scope

- Player skill modeling.
- Adaptive difficulty.
- UI hints.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every clue type is documented.
- [ ] Difficulty is computed from a deterministic measure.
- [ ] Buckets have numeric thresholds.
- [ ] The solver reports the measure.
- [ ] Generated puzzles land in the requested bucket or are regenerated.
- [ ] Fixtures cover each bucket.

## Plan

- [ ] Define the measure.
- [ ] Calibrate thresholds on fixtures.
- [ ] Expose the measure from the solver.
- [ ] Document the buckets.

## Validation

- [ ] The same puzzle gets the same difficulty.
- [ ] A trivial puzzle and a hard puzzle land in different buckets.
- [ ] Generation respects the requested bucket.

## References

- Generator: #4
- Solver oracle: #4
- Tests: ops/templates#34
